title: Path Operations
description: Reshape paths after drawing: noise, simplify, fit, hull, and stroke-to-outline.

bubble.title: Path Operations
bubble.body: Five operations that reshape a path after it is drawn: Noise, Simplify, Fit, Hull, and Stroke to Outline. They act on the selected path — draw first, operate second.

bubble.title: Watch: noise roughens a path
bubble.body: Press Watch demo: the program draws a rectangle and points at the section. The Noise button itself is a panel press — the do-steps below put it in your hands.

demo.title: A smooth path
demo.body: Drawing a rectangle — straight edges, four corners.

demo.title: Noise lives here
demo.body: Noise would displace this outline's points by a seeded random amount — same seed, same roughness, every time. Open the preview box for the button and its amount.

bubble.title: Draw a point-rich path
bubble.body: Steer to one end of a diameter and press M to start a circle. Circles carry many points — exactly what Simplify needs.

bubble.title: Deposit it
bubble.body: Steer to the other end of the diameter and press M again. Leave the circle selected — the operations need a selection.

bubble.title: Apply Simplify
bubble.body: Open the Path Operations preview, choose Simplify, and click Simplify path. The circle's redundant points are removed — the outline barely moves, but the path underneath gets much simpler.

bubble.title: The five operations
bubble.body: Noise displaces points with seeded randomness. Simplify removes points. Fit re-fits a smooth curve through a path. Hull wraps the points in a concave hull. Stroke to Outline turns a stroked path into the outline shape itself. Pick one in the bar; its settings open from the preview box.
